about:
Tri-Steel Manufacturing Co. was founded in 1962 in Grand Forks, North Dakota, by Adolph (Toby) Tobiason, Milton Homstad, and Louis Peabody. The company began by manufacturing and repairing machinery for the potato and agricultural industries in the Red River Valley spanning North Dakota and Minnesota.

Today, Tri-Steel operates as a full-service manufacturer with capabilities spanning administration, marketing, engineering, procurement, and production. Its primary business is the design and manufacture of potato equipment, including Logan Potato Equipment, and complete processing lines that move produce from field to final consumer packaging. The company also produces individual parts and finished equipment for supply chains in wind energy, power generation, grain handling, and general contract manufacturing. A full-service machine shop and a large steel inventory support both production and retail sales, while an MRO division distributes replacement parts from brands such as Browning, TECO Westinghouse, Rexnord, Morse, Carlisle, Timken, and Lovejoy.

Tri-Steel serves the potato and agricultural sectors across the Red River Valley, as well as customers in wind energy, power generation, and grain handling. Its contract manufacturing work extends to diverse industrial supply chains, and its MRO distribution supports local and regional maintenance operations.

The company emphasizes its integrated approach, combining design, engineering, procurement, and manufacturing under one roof to deliver complete equipment solutions and rapid parts availability.
